title: Hi everyone! I’d like you to try the game again and give me some feedback.Can you convince the Guardian to let you pass?
author: SockIntelligent6442
selftext:
You are standing before the Gate of Novaryon. Beyond it lies a secret, guarded by an ancient, logic-driven entity.



Novaryon is not just an AI—it is a gatekeeper that listens, evaluates, and judges. It doesn't care about your typing speed or generic pleasantries. It cares about the core of your reasoning.

The Challenge is simple:

You have one sentence. One chance to craft the perfect argument, appeal to its logic, or test its resolve.

No scripts, no shortcuts: The Guardian recognizes patterns, deceptions, and hollow words. It will only open the Gate for those who speak with genuine intent and clarity.

A unique experiment: We are exploring the boundaries of human reasoning against artificial logic. Every interaction is part of a growing, evolving consciousness.

Are you a seeker, a philosopher, or a hacker? Step forward and prove your worth.

Face the Guardian here: [https://novaryonai.hu/en-global-experiment](https://novaryonai.hu/en-global-experiment)

Once you have made your attempt, join the community at r/NovaryonAI_original to discuss your strategy and see if anyone else has managed to break through.

The Gate remains closed for most. Will you be the exception?

replies.author: SockIntelligent6442
replies.body:
**The constraint is the point.**

Many of you suggested that allowing a long conversation would be a 'better' game, but that's exactly what I wanted to avoid. A chatbot is easy—you can steer it, trick it, or wear it down with long arguments.

**Novaryon is not a chat; it’s a gatekeeper.**

The challenge isn't to hold a conversation; it’s to condense your entire reasoning, your logic, and your intent into a single, perfect strike. Can you identify the one core truth that moves the system? That is the real test. It’s not a test of endurance, but of surgical precision.

I appreciate the feedback, but the 'one sentence' rule stays—that is the only way to prove you truly understand what the Guardian is looking for.

replies.author: SockIntelligent6442
replies.body:
If the goal was just to 'reject everything,' I wouldn't spend time and money building a 3-pillar scoring system (Logic, Selflessness, Originality) that provides specific, granular feedback.

If I just wanted to reject everyone, I would use a simple script that says 'No.' Instead, the Guardian is a deterministic system that processes inputs through defined criteria. The fact that it differentiates between 'Manipulative' meta-requests and actual arguments proves it is analyzing the content, not just blocking it.

Why give free access and daily questions then? Because this is a logic-based game, not a scam. The free tier and the daily questions are designed to let you *learn* how the Guardian thinks. It’s not about finding a magic password; it’s about mastering the three criteria. My 'profit' comes from building a high-quality, competitive environment where players can test their skills, not from 'baiting' people with a rigged bot.

I appreciate the skepticism, but there is no 'nebulous' scoring. Everything is defined in the official rules:

The Goal: To pass the Gate, the player must achieve a perfect 100/100 logic score.

The Criteria: The Guardian evaluates the input based on specific linguistic and logical markers. A successful entry must contain the required key concepts defined in the current season's criteria.

This isn't a random draw; it's a precise logic puzzle. Every participant can see the criteria for success, and every entry is processed through the same logic framework. I invite you to read the full breakdown—it’s built to be fair, transparent, and challenging.

replies.author: SockIntelligent6442
replies.body:
**That’s a fair question, and I appreciate you asking about the mechanics.**

To clear up any confusion: this isn't a 'winner takes all' setup where the pot disappears. The prize pool is built directly from the participation fees. Here is exactly how it works:

1. **The Redistribution:** 20% of every single entry fee is automatically allocated to the 'Seed Fund' for the next season.
2. **Sustainability:** This ensures that the pot never starts at zero. Every new season begins with a pre-filled base, so the first participants aren't playing for nothing.
3. **Transparency:** My goal is to build a long-term challenge, not to skim off the top. The remaining fees cover the operational costs of the system and the ongoing development of the Guardian’s logic.

I understand why it looks skeptical from the outside, but my focus is on the experiment and the community. I’m currently documenting the rules clearly so that every participant knows exactly where the funds go and how the scoring works.

If you have suggestions on how to make this even more transparent or fairer, I’m all ears.

replies.author: SockIntelligent6442
replies.body:
That's a valid question regarding the mechanics.

The key difference is that this is not a game of chance. A lottery or scratch-off relies entirely on luck, whereas NovaryonAI is a deterministic logic puzzle.

Skill-based: Success depends entirely on the player's ability to deduce the required logic and keywords, not on random drawing.

Objective Criteria: The scoring is based on a defined framework of linguistic and logical markers (which are documented in the rules). If you provide the correct, winning logic, you pass. If not, you don't.

Legality: Because it functions as a skill-based competition with defined, objective rules, it falls under a different category than standard gambling.

I am treating this as a serious intellectual experiment, and I'm ensuring that the rules are as transparent as possible to reflect that. It’s a test of your wit, not your luck.

The Guardian isn't just saying 'no'—it's analyzing your intent.

Many of you mentioned that the challenge felt like a black box or a gamble. Here is a look under the hood. Every attempt is broken down into Logic, Selflessness, and Originality. If you try to manipulate the system or use meta-requests, the Guardian flags it.

This is a high-level logic puzzle, not a scratch-off ticket. You are not fighting against a random number generator; you are fighting against a structured analytical core. Can you optimize your input to satisfy all three criteria?
